title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 95-98). X is a (metrisable) stratified space with strata indexed by an ordered set I. X_i^* is the open star of stratum i. V_i is a 'prévoisinage tubulaire' of X_i^*, and V_{i0...in} = V_{i0} ∩ ... ∩ V_{in} for a flag i0<...<in. The implicit hypothesis is that V_i ∩ V_j = ∅ unless i and j are comparable. On p.96 Grothendieck replaces single indices by 'bandes', i.e. intervals/segments J of I. He sets V_J = V(X_J^*, X) = ∪_{j∈J} V_j = colim_{d∈Drap(J)} V_d, and V_J^Z = V_J ∩ Z. Claim (100), marked 'à vérifier' on p.96: V^Z_d ↪ V_d is a homotopy equivalence when Z ⊃ X^*_{i_n}.

This page:
(105) V_J^Z = ∪_j V_j^Z = colim_{d∈Drap(J)} V_d^Z. Each term maps by a homotopy equivalence (the mark '≀|(h)') to V_d as soon as Z ⊃ X_J^*. This is the input for a gluing argument showing V_J^Z ≃ V_J.
(106) For two bandes J, L he defines:
- V_{J,L} = V_J ∩ V_L;
- V_{J,L}^Z = V_{J,L} ∩ Z;
- V_{J,L}^L = V_J ∩ X_L^*. This equals V_{J,L} ∩ X_L^* because X_L^* ⊂ V_L, so it is the case Z = X_L^* of notation (102).
A marginal 'suggestion' proposes a decorated symbol V^↳_{J,L} instead, with V^↳_{i0...in} = V_{i0...in}^{X^*_{in}} = V_{i0} ∩ ... ∩ V_{in} ∩ X^*_{in}.
(107) Distributivity gives V_{J,L} = ∪_{j∈J,l∈L} V_j ∩ V_l. Splitting into j=l, j<l and l<j gives ∪_{i∈J∩L} V_i ∪ ∪_{j<l} V_{jl} ∪ ∪_{l<j} V_{lj}. This also equals colim V_d over flags d in J∪L meeting both J and L. The struck-out variant 'Drap_{≥2}' is rightly discarded, since one-element flags in J∩L must count.
(108) If J ≤ L, the third union disappears. Bottom-right NB: such flags have all elements in J forming an initial segment and all elements in L a final segment, with i0∈J and in∈L. The footnote apparently notes that the first union is empty when J∩L = ∅.

Purpose: build a 'Čech-type' cover of neighbourhoods of unions of consecutive strata, indexed by flags. Each piece retracts by homotopy equivalence onto its trace on a closed star. Gluing these equivalences over the open cover (the next page's (110), (111), (113)) gives the homotopy-theoretic skeleton of the 'déploiement' (unfolding) of a stratified space.
errors: Colimit = union is valid only because, for each point x, the flags d with x∈V_d are the subchains of the chain {i : x∈V_i}. This needs V_i∩V_j = ∅ for incomparable i, j (or I totally ordered); the assumption is implicit. The subposet of such subchains meeting both J and L is connected and closed under unions, so the colimit is the union.

Passing from termwise homotopy equivalences (100) to (105)/(110) needs a homotopy-colimit/gluing argument for numerable open covers (Segal/Dold type). Grothendieck only gestures at this ('on suppose X métrisable'), and (100) itself is still flagged 'à vérifier' on p.96.
The condition in (105) only needs Z ⊃ X^*_{i_n} for all last elements of flags in J, which follows from Z ⊃ X_J^*. This is consistent, just not spelled out.
The NB about initial/final segments requires J ≤ L in the interval-order sense (inf J ≤ inf L and sup J ≤ sup L). With that reading it is correct.

ideas.what: Neighbourhoods V_J of unions of strata over an interval J of the stratification poset, written as a colimit of flag-indexed intersections V_d over Drap(J)
ideas.modern_name: Čech/nerve-type decomposition of a system of tubular neighbourhoods (control data à la Mather/Thom) indexed by the subdivision poset of chains
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom (1969), Mather (1970) for control data; colimit-over-chains formalism in later homotopy theory of stratified spaces (Quinn 1988, Lurie HA App. A, Ayala-Francis-Tanaka)
ideas.where_published: Only the vague programme in Esquisse d'un programme (1984, §5-6 on tame topology and 'déploiement')

ideas.what: Formula V_J ∩ V_L as a colimit over flags in J∪L meeting both J and L, with the J-part an initial and the L-part a final segment
ideas.modern_name: Join/concatenation decomposition of chains in an ordinal sum; elementary poset combinatorics of the subdivision

ideas.what: Homotopy invariance V^Z_{J,L} ↪ V_{J,L} when Z contains the open star X_L^*, obtained by gluing termwise homotopy equivalences over an open cover
ideas.modern_name: Gluing lemma / homotopy colimits over numerable open covers; deformation retraction of tubular neighbourhoods onto links/closed stars

missed.claim: These interval-indexed tubular neighbourhoods, used to 'déployer' a stratified space, are a concrete, point-set precursor of the 'unzipping' of conically smooth stratified spaces into manifolds with corners (Ayala-Francis-Tanaka). They also anticipate homotopy-link/exit-path presentations of stratified homotopy types, which use the same kind of chain-indexed (flag-indexed) diagrams. This single page is only a bookkeeping step in that programme.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents how Grothendieck organized the unfolding combinatorially via flags of strata and intervals ('bandes'). This is of historical interest for crediting the déploiement idea mentioned in Esquisse, but the page itself contains no new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine set-theoretic and combinatorial bookkeeping (distributivity, chains in a union of intervals) supporting a gluing argument. Its interest is only as part of Grothendieck's otherwise unpublished stratified-space programme.
transcription_corrections: The decoration under V_d in (105) is '≀|(h)' (homotopy equivalence), not '(4)'.
The marginal suggestion symbol looks like a hooked arrow 'V^↳_{J,L}', not '♮'. It reads: 'Suggestion : V^↳_{J,L} au lieu de V^L_J ; V^↳_{i0...in} = V^{X^*_{in}}_{i0...in} = V_{i0...in} ∩ X^*_{in}'.

In the second line of (106) the superscript on the right is a struck letter replaced by X_L^*, with the annotation '... où Z = X_L^*' below; under V_J ∩ X_L^* it reads '" V_J^{X_L^*} ... notation (102)'.
In the struck term of (107) the index line reads 'j∈J, l∈L, j≤l' (not 'j≤L').
The footnote seems to say that the first union (over J∩L) is empty, i.e. reduces to ∅, if J∩L = ∅. The page number at the bottom left is 97.
'bandes' is the right reading of the repeated word ('deux bandes J et L', 'J et L des bandes').
